basis: Defining myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia; intellectual disability 1/2. Retinopathy 1/2 omitted at cap; restrictive ventilation may reflect myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 1/2 supports direct neurodevelopmental impairment; prioritized at the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: none: pigmentary retinopathy in 1/2 qualifies, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of substantial neurodevelopmental impairment.

basis: Juvenile neurodegenerative parkinsonism; scoliosis and pes cavus occur in 30-79%, but reflect motor dysfunction rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis/pes cavus are frequent (30-79%) secondary deformities; rigidity and dystonia are neurologic, without established direct skeletal disease.

basis: Anterior-segment dysgenesis defines type 2; dental anomalies are reported without frequencies. Common dental, auditory, cardiac or CNS dysfunction is not established for this subtype.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: hypodontia/microdontia are reported, but type 2 prevalence >=30% or status as major diagnostic criteria is not established.

basis: Adenovirus infection umbrella spans respiratory, ocular, intestinal and urinary syndromes; direct pulmonary damage in >=30% across the group is not established.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory illness is one of several presentations; damaging respiratory involvement in >=30% across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Defining cardiac/skeletal syndrome; ptosis 14/16; cutis laxa/hyperkeratosis 4/7. Coagulation findings (PTT 2/2, factor XI deficiency 1/3) omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: PTT prolongation 2/2 and reduced factor XI 1/3 support involvement, but omitted at cap; ocular and skin abnormalities have stronger prevalence evidence.
decisions.ocular: involved: congenital ptosis affects 14/16 (88%); eyelids belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Eyelid malformations define BPES. Ovarian failure affects type I females; amenorrhea 2/3 in a sex-limited sample does not establish >=30% across both types and sexes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ovarian failure is restricted to type I females; amenorrhea 2/3 does not establish >=30% involvement across the BPES umbrella.

basis: Eye/lung malformations and intellectual disability (80-99%) define the phenotype; cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%. Most renal/GI defects are occasional.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiovascular malformations occur in 30-79%; eye/lung and near-universal neurodevelopmental involvement take the three primary slots.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly in the definition and occurs in 80-99%, making neurodevelopmental impairment a major defining feature.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; cutis laxa 5/5, global developmental delay 4/5 and oligodontia 1/2 support additional axes. Dental prevalence rests on a small sample; reflux is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: oligodontia in 1/2 (50%) is direct congenital dental loss; teeth belong to this axis. Small sample lowers confidence; reflux alone would not qualify.

basis: Inherited organic acid metabolism disorders; direct metabolic brain injury/developmental impairment affects roughly >=30% across typical clinical forms; benign subtypes vary.

decisions.neurologic: involved: lasting toxic/metabolic brain injury and developmental impairment affect roughly >=30% across the common clinical organic acidurias; benign subtypes are exceptions.

basis: Defining intellectual disability and skeletal malformations; primary hypothyroidism and hypospadias each occur in 30-79%. Hypospadias affects urethra; other genital findings lack an axis.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a congenital urethral malformation reported in 30-79%; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra, despite its genital presentation.
